name: LogicGame
intro: LogicGame是一个旨在评估大型语言模型（LLM）基于规则的推理能力的基准。它通过提供多样化的游戏场景，要求模型理解并应用预定义的规则来解决问题，从而将其逻辑推理能力与先验知识分离开来。该基准不仅评估最终结果，也关注中间步骤，并涵盖了从简单到复杂的不同难度级别。
build_method: 广泛调研与众包, 专家人工原创与质控, 执行/规划双域规则题, 四级难度与双语翻译
metric: AP-Acc, A-Acc, P-Acc, IFError, JSError, NIJ-Acc
task_type: Agent任务, 规划, 生成
eval_feature: 过程导向, 双语, 分域分难度, 部分隐藏参考
scale: 304道底层题目×中英双语；执行180、规划124；每级76题；当前公开whole为每语304条 qid/contexts/level/category 输入，dev为每语10条带参考示例
build_method_en: Research and crowdsourcing, expert human authoring and QC, Execution/Planning rule games, four levels and bilingual translation
eval_feature_en: Process-oriented, bilingual, domain-and-level reporting, partly hidden references
intro_en: LogicGame is a benchmark designed to evaluate the rule-based reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs). It presents diverse game scenarios that require models to understand and apply predefined rules to solve problems, thereby separating their logical reasoning from prior knowledge. The benchmark assesses not only the final outcomes but also intermediate steps, covering a range of difficulty levels from simple to complex.
scale_en: 304 underlying problems × Chinese/English; 180 Execution and 124 Planning; 76 per level; current public whole has 304 qid/contexts/level/category input rows per language and dev has 10 referenced examples per language
metric_en: AP-Acc, A-Acc, P-Acc, IFError, JSError, NIJ-Acc

drawio_review_note: Paper-alignment review passed on 2026-07-21 against arXiv:2408.15778v4 (submitted 2024-08-28, latest revision 2024-10-12), Sections 3.1–3.2 and Appendices A–C, plus official data commit 4884edb6de726fe35debb656215ef429cd7e2f4d dated 2025-03-31. LogicGame begins with extensive research and crowdsourcing of rule-following real-world scenarios, then gamifies them; expert human annotators author novel out-of-domain problems intended to be unavailable online, minimize dependence on natural-language inference, and require no knowledge beyond the supplied rules. Execution contains deterministic single-step inference with every intermediate step verifiable; Planning seeks any valid strategic multi-step solution rather than an optimal one and introduces checkpoints or state variables where appropriate. The paper gives 304 underlying bilingual problems: 180 Execution across 19 named subcategories and 124 Planning across 12, with 76 problems per level (45 Execution plus 31 Planning) for levels 0–3. It does not disclose annotator count or recruitment, leakage-search and rejection procedure, agreement or adjudication, category-specific generation templates, rejection rates, or reference-checker implementation. Each item receives a final-answer reference and, when required, a step-by-step process. The JSON contract always uses an answer list of strings; levels 1–3 and some multi-step level-0 items also require a process list, while simple single-step level-0 items can be answer-only. Difficulty increases through both rule complexity and reasoning-step count. Two worked exemplars per question contain the question, answer, process, and explanation. Questions are authored first in Chinese and then translated with their instructions into English. The pinned public repository is a data-only Apache-2.0 release: en_all_304.jsonl and zh_all_304.jsonl expose 304 prompt rows per language with qid, contexts, level, and category but omit references and examples; the two 10-row dev files add references and two examples. The README says the languages correspond directly, but current language-specific qids differ and file order does not align, and no explicit bilingual pair key is released. Release history drifted from 60-item dev plus 244-item test per language to 10-item demonstration dev plus complete 304-input whole files; the 2025 commit then corrected one English and one Chinese prompt annotation. Paper evaluation prompts with rules, optional 0/1/2 exemplars inserted before the question, and the item-specific JSON constraint; generation uses temperature 0, max 2,048 tokens, and provider defaults otherwise, while model-specific system/chat wrappers are undisclosed. The paper and official Codabench evaluation pages define an explicit two-stage order: first extract JSON context from the model response; if none can be extracted, count IFError; otherwise parse the extracted context into formal JSON; if parsing fails, count JSError. Only successfully parsed JSON proceeds to A/P/AP scoring. The extractor and parser implementations remain private and are not released in GitHub. Answer Accuracy is binary, Process Accuracy is character-level (set equal to answer accuracy for answer-only level-0 items), and Answer Process Accuracy is their logical AND; Figure 2 maps A-Acc = 1 and P-Acc = 0.83 to AP-Acc = 0, so AP-Acc is one only when both are exactly one. NIJ-Acc is AP-Acc divided by one minus both error rates. Answer normalization, the character-similarity function, hidden whole-set references, and the evaluator implementation are not released in GitHub. Scores are reported by language, domain, and level; the overall language score is the mean over all 304 problems, and the paper also averages Chinese and English results. The original Codabench competition 4140, created 2024-10-10, now directs participants encountering running bugs to LogicGame-v2 competition 6934, created 2025-03-31, whose official description calls it the bugs-fixed version. Both portals keep reference_data and scoring_program private. GitHub publishes 14-model EN/ZH tables, but whole-set labels and scoring assets remain withheld, so the benchmark is partly public rather than fully reproducible offline.
